artifacts.summary: Determines, via the postflight consumer's own log line and the handoff-schema.md settled-decision table, that research agents must never write .orchestrator-handoff.json; identifies all 21 research-agent contract files (core + 15 extensions) that currently contradict this with an unconditional MUST-write instruction, and flags an adjacent out-of-scope instance in planner-agent.md/general-implementation-agent.md.

memory_candidates.content: orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's own log line at the absent-handoff recovery branch states the design assumption directly: base-mode research/plan/implement dispatches never write .orchestrator-handoff.json, and recovery relies entirely on .return-meta.json. When reconciling a docs-vs-agent-contract conflict about handoff-writer obligations, treat this executable log line (not just docs/architecture/handoff-schema.md) as the authoritative tie-breaker.

A boilerplate contract section (e.g. the .orchestrator-handoff.json orchestrator-mode-dispatches section) that was copy-templated across many agent files can silently drift out of sync with a later architecture-doc decision, because fixing the doc does not fan the fix back out to every templated copy. When investigating a doc-vs-contract conflict in one agent file, grep for the same section heading across all sibling agent files (by filename pattern, e.g. *-research-agent.md) before assuming the conflict is isolated.

orchestrator_mode_note: This dispatch carried orchestrator_mode: true, but per this report's own finding, base-mode research agents must never write .orchestrator-handoff.json (confirmed by orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's own recovery log line and by docs/architecture/handoff-schema.md's settled-decision table). No .orchestrator-handoff.json was written for this dispatch, deliberately, consistent with the recommended fix -- not an oversight. Outcome recovery is via this .return-meta.json file.
